title: Word Count, Longest Word, Capitalise
statement: You are given one line of text. Words are separated by one or more spaces. The line may start or end with spaces. Print three lines. Line 1: the number of words. Line 2: the longest word, as it was written. If two words tie, print the first one. Line 3: every word with its first letter in capital and the other letters in small letters, joined by a single space.
inputFormat: One line with English letters and spaces. It has at least one word.
outputFormat: Three lines: the word count, the longest word, and the capitalised line.
constraints: The line has only letters (a-z, A-Z) and spaces
The line has at least one word
explanations: There are 4 words. Hello and world both have 5 letters, so the first one, hello, is printed.
Extra spaces at the start, end and middle are ignored. Output words are joined by one space, and FUN becomes Fun.
reference:
import sys

line = sys.stdin.readline()
words = line.split()
best = words[0]
for w in words:
    if len(w) > len(best):
        best = w
print(len(words))
print(best)
print(" ".join(w[0].upper() + w[1:].lower() for w in words))
